input.strategy_title: GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Platform teams fund shared GPU clusters but cannot attribute consumption to the
projects using them, so capacity costs are socialized and heavy users have no
incentive to release resources. The in-flight metering strategy
(RHAISTRAT-9990) is delivering per-project GPU-hour usage data; this strategy
builds the administrator-facing chargeback reporting on top of that data. The
metering data schema is owned by RHAISTRAT-9990 and is not final until that
strategy lands — reporting work here consumes it, and must not re-implement
collection.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can view per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, computed from the metering data delivered by RHAISTRAT-9990. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Reports can be exported as CSV and retrieved via a stable API for finance tooling. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard admin view shows current-month consumption against each project's Kueue quota. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) and export integration. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- The metering collection pipeline itself (RHAISTRAT-9990)
- Currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars

## Open Questions

1. The metering data schema finalizes only when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; report
   implementation consuming it carries that external timing risk.

# Per-project GPU-hour chargeback reporting backend (Tier 1)

## Description

This epic delivers the reporting backend for administrator-facing GPU chargeback:
computation of per-project GPU-hour consumption aggregates over selectable time
ranges from the metering data delivered by the in-flight GPU usage metering work
(RHAISTRAT-9990), exposed through a stable report retrieval API with CSV export
for finance tooling. A schema-isolation layer confines every reference to the
metering data schema so that schema changes from the in-flight metering strategy
are absorbed in one place. Metering collection itself is consumed, never
re-implemented. This is Tier 1 work: it builds against the current draft metering
schema behind the isolation layer so it does not wait for the metering strategy
to land.

## Scope

- Report computation producing per-project GPU-hour consumption aggregates over
  selectable time ranges, sourced from the metering data delivered by
  RHAISTRAT-9990.
- A schema-isolation layer that confines all metering-schema references
  (mappings from metering data fields to the report model), validated against
  the current draft schema.
- A stable report retrieval API suitable for programmatic consumers such as
  finance tooling.
- CSV export of the same report data.
- Report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) applied consistently with the
  metering data's semantics.

Out of scope: the metering collection pipeline (RHAISTRAT-9990) and
currency/cost-rate modelling — reports are in GPU-hours, not dollars.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given metering data, per-project GPU-hour consumption aggregates are computable
  for selectable time ranges, and the metering data is consumed rather than
  re-implemented (no collection-side pipeline code is added).
- All references to the metering data schema are confined to the isolation layer,
  verified by a structural check or test; the layer is validated against the
  current draft schema.
- Reports are retrievable as CSV and via the stable report API by a non-UI
  client.
- Aggregate outputs are deterministic and reproducible for a fixed time range and
  fixed input data, verified by a test with fixture data.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
  ranges — computation and retrieval portion.
- HLR-2 (P1, bundled): CSV export and stable API for finance tooling — bundled
  with HLR-1 because it is a presentation mode of the same report data surface
  and API, for the same component and team; splitting would build the same
  surface twice.

## Risks / Notes

- The metering data schema is not final until RHAISTRAT-9990 lands; the
  isolation layer is the containment for that risk, and final-schema alignment
  is deferred to dedicated follow-on work gated on that strategy landing.

# Dashboard admin view for GPU chargeback reports (Tier 1)

## Description

This epic delivers the administrator-facing Dashboard view for GPU chargeback:
per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges, and
current-month consumption displayed against each project's Kueue quota. The view
consumes the report retrieval surface provided by the platform's reporting
backend; it does not compute reports or re-implement metering. This is Tier 1
work, buildable against the report API contract without waiting for the metering
strategy to land.

## Scope

- An administrator-facing section in the Dashboard surfacing per-project GPU-hour
  consumption reports with selectable time ranges.
- Current-month consumption displayed alongside each project's Kueue quota, with
  quota information read from the platform's existing queueing configuration.
- Access control for the view limited to platform administrators, using the
  Dashboard's existing authentication and RBAC integration.

Out of scope: report computation, the report API, and CSV export (owned by the
reporting backend).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the reporting capability is available, administrators can view
  per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time ranges in the
  Dashboard.
- Current-month consumption is displayed against each project's Kueue quota for
  every project with quota or consumption data.
- The view is not accessible to non-administrator users, verified against the
  Dashboard's RBAC.
- The view renders data retrieved from the report retrieval surface without
  duplicating report computation logic.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports over selectable time
  ranges — administrator viewing portion.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): current-month consumption against each project's Kueue
  quota — bundled with HLR-1's viewing portion because it renders in the same
  Dashboard admin view over the same report data; splitting would duplicate the
  view surface.

# Align GPU-hour reporting to the final metering data schema (Tier 2)

## Description

This epic aligns GPU chargeback reporting to the final metering data schema once
the in-flight GPU usage metering strategy (RHAISTRAT-9990) lands: it updates or
retires the schema-isolation layer built by the Tier 1 reporting work and
verifies report semantics and outputs against the delivered data. It completes
the reporting capability in final form so that per-project GPU-hour reports
reflect the metering data as actually shipped.

## Scope

- Update the schema-isolation layer to consume the final metering data schema,
  or remove it if the final schema matches the draft the layer was built against.
- Verify per-project GPU-hour aggregates and the CSV/API report outputs against
  delivered metering data.
- Confirm applied report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) match the final
  schema's semantics.

Out of scope: any change to the metering collection pipeline itself, and
currency/cost-rate modelling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reports compute correctly against the final metering data schema, with the
  isolation layer updated or removed accordingly.
- Report outputs (view data, CSV, API) are verified for consistency against
  delivered metering data.
- No references to superseded draft-schema constructs remain outside the
  isolation layer, verified by a structural check or test.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): per-project GPU-hour consumption reports — final-form computation
  against the delivered metering data schema.

## Risks / Notes

- Start is gated by an external precondition: RHAISTRAT-9990 must land and its
  data schema be final. That timing is controlled by the metering strategy and
  cannot be compressed here; it is a scheduling precondition, not an acceptance
  criterion. If the final schema differs materially from the draft, the
  isolation layer absorbs the change within the reporting backend.

# Documentation for GPU chargeback report semantics and export integration

## Description

This epic delivers user-facing documentation for the GPU chargeback reporting
capability as built: what the reports mean and how finance tooling integrates
with the export surface. It runs last so the content describes the implemented
capability, including its final metering-data semantics.

## Scope

- Report semantics topic: what counts as a GPU-hour, time-range semantics, and
  how consumption is attributed per project.
- Export integration topic: retrieving reports via the stable report API and as
  CSV for finance tooling.
- Usage coverage of the Dashboard administrator view for consumption reports and
  the quota comparison.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers report semantics (GPU-hour definition, time-range and
  per-project attribution semantics) and export integration (API and CSV
  retrieval).
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reporting
  capability and Dashboard view, with review sign-off recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation covers report semantics (what counts as a
  GPU-hour) and export integration.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9018 (GPU chargeback reporting for platform administrators)

## Triage Outcome

Full decomposition (not below-threshold, not docs-only): the strategy spans two
components owned by two different teams (Dashboard — RHOAI Dashboard; Distributed
Workloads — Distributed Workloads), and its single open question is an external
dependency with uncertain timing (the metering data schema owned by in-flight
RHAISTRAT-9990), which requires tiered delivery rather than a single epic.

## Strategy Parsing Notes

- **Affected Components**: Dashboard, Distributed Workloads (listed without
  per-component change detail — inferred from HLRs, see mapping below).
- **Impacted Teams table**: missing from the strategy. Teams inferred from
  `.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/` owning teams:
  Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard; Distributed Workloads → Distributed Workloads.
- **Dependencies table**: missing as a table; the frontmatter carries

- **Staff Engineer Input**: absent — no overrides to log.

These missing sections are recorded as health warnings (below); decomposition
proceeded with available information.

## Step 1.5 — Staff Engineer Input

No Staff Engineer Input section present in the strategy; nothing to override.

## Component Graph and Mapping

Both affected components are in the platform (architecture context files exist):
`dashboard.md` and `distributed-workloads.md` under
`.context/architecture-context/architecture/rhoai-3.0/`. Both are Konflux
onboarded, so no onboarding chain is generated.

| Strategy component | Change | Owner team | Classification | Canonical component |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Distributed Workloads | Report computation from metering data, stable report API + CSV export; final-schema alignment | Distributed Workloads | Active | Distributed Workloads |
| Dashboard | Administrator view of consumption reports and quota comparison | RHOAI Dashboard | Active | Dashboard |
| Documentation (implied by HLR-4) | Report semantics and export integration docs | Distributed Workloads (inferred — content is the reporting backend's domain) | Active (content authoring) | Documentation |

**Non-obvious mapping logged:** the strategy does not state which component hosts
the report computation and stable API. It is assigned to Distributed Workloads
(the metering/GPU domain) because the Dashboard's architecture context states the
Dashboard's only interface is the Kubernetes API — it owns no data plane and
exposes no private component APIs — so a stable API for finance tooling cannot
live in the Dashboard. The Dashboard epic consumes the report surface.

## Investigation Assessment

The strategy's single open question — the metering data schema finalizes only
when RHAISTRAT-9990 lands — was evaluated against the Step 3 decision rule. The
resolution is controlled by a third party (the in-flight metering strategy), not
by any experiment this strategy can run: no Investigation epic can resolve it
faster. Per the external-dependency rule, it is modeled as a precondition with
tiered delivery (Step 5.5): partial value is deliverable by building Tier 1
against the current draft schema behind a schema-isolation layer, with Tier 2
performing final-schema alignment once RHAISTRAT-9990 lands. No Investigation
epic is generated; the residual risk is a health warning.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9018-E001 reporting backend] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9018-E002 Dashboard admin view]
    E001 --> E003[RHAISTRAT-9018-E003 final-schema alignment]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 12/13 (framework/API producer → consumer serial) | The Dashboard view's code builds against the report API and data model produced by the reporting backend epic; consuming code cannot be written against an API that does not exist. |
| E001 → E003 | Tiered delivery (Step 5.5 / Rule 18) | Tier 2 alignment reworks the schema-isolation layer the Tier 1 epic builds; it cannot start before that layer exists, and it is additionally gated by the external precondition that RHAISTRAT-9990 has landed (Risks/Notes on E003, not an AC — externally controlled timing). |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by all Implementations) | Documentation describes the reporting capability as built. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 | Documentation covers the Dashboard admin view as built. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 | Documentation of report semantics (what counts as a GPU-hour) must reflect the final metering schema, so docs land after the Tier 2 alignment. |

E002 and E003 are deliberately parallel: the Tier 2 alignment changes how the
reporting backend consumes the metering schema internally, not the report API
contract the Dashboard consumes (that is the purpose of the isolation layer).

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |

Splitting would build the same API/data structures twice and add an artificial serialization edge; the pair is one capability at the higher priority (P0). |

Not separately schedulable without duplicating the view. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Tiered Delivery

- **Tier 1 (independent, start now)**: E001 (report computation, isolation layer
  against the current draft schema, stable API + CSV) and E002 (Dashboard admin
  view). Delivers administrator-visible consumption reporting without waiting for
  the metering strategy to land.
- **Tier 2 (dependency-gated)**: E003 — final-schema alignment, gated by the
  external precondition that RHAISTRAT-9990 has landed and its schema is final.

- **Missing strategy sections**: Impacted Teams table, Dependencies table,

  Workloads) and the inferred placement of the report API in Distributed
  Workloads rather than the Dashboard.

  split and the schema-isolation layer; the residual risk is rework in E003 if
  the final schema diverges materially from the draft. E003's start date is
  externally controlled and cannot be compressed by this strategy.
- **Priority notes**: E003 is P0 because it completes HLR-1 (P0) in final form,
  even though it is Tier 2 and gated on external timing — planners should not
  read its P0 as "start immediately". E004 is P1 (docs-authoring exception:

- **Scope boundary enforced as AC**: the metering collection pipeline
  (RHAISTRAT-9990) is out of scope; E001 carries an explicit AC that metering is
  consumed, not re-implemented.
- No epic exceeds the ~2-week guideline; no re-split triggers required.
